TU/e Research Data Support

Assess and Prepare Research Data for Reuse and Repository Deposit

The FAIR Data Clinic starts with one reuse-readiness assessment workflow. It assesses the files, documentation, metadata, provenance, software, rights, and other evidence in the research package so researchers can improve it independently, request Data Steward assistance when useful, or continue to repository preflight when no professional block remains.

Why test material is required: file contents are processed locally, but this proof of concept is not an approved secure service. Browser storage is not encrypted, case metadata and findings may remain on the workstation, and the application has not completed institutional privacy, security, or production-deployment approval. Use fictitious contact details and non-sensitive or explicitly approved files.
Why there is a Data Steward workspace: routine reuse-readiness preparation can remain researcher self-service. The Data Steward workspace supports requested assistance and professional-review conditions that require judgment or specialist routing. Selecting this workspace does not authenticate the user or confer institutional authority.

Processing, storage, and transfer limits

Local browser-analysis thresholds

Local file selection has no toolkit-imposed maximum file size or total package size. Checksum and content-inspection thresholds protect browser performance and may cause large files to be sampled or skipped by particular checks; they do not prevent those files from being selected and do not represent repository upload limits. The current checksum mode is shown above. Selected files can only be embedded in a generated ZIP when the package is 100 MB or less.

Repository and institutional limits

Repository storage allocations, free-volume thresholds, charges, and transfer routes are separate. For 4TU.ResearchData, confirm current TU/e arrangements and large-package transfer requirements with the local front office before deposit.

Cross-artifact schema

Needs improvementRelevant evidence exists, but it is incomplete, weak, or insufficient for practical reuse.
MissingExpected applicable evidence was not found.

Criterion-Level Reassessment Comparison

Evidence-based documentation progress

README Documentation Completeness

Measure coverage of applicable README documentation elements against the actual locally assessed README. This is not a FAIR score, dataset-quality score, readiness percentage, legal determination, or repository-acceptance decision.

Deterministic metadata quality control

Cross-Artifact Consistency

Compare the README with the structured public metadata, Schema.org JSON-LD, and file manifest. Individual consistency rules remain unscored and do not issue an approval decision. README Documentation Completeness is calculated separately as evidence coverage, not FAIRness or readiness.

Evidence boundary: The selected README is read locally. The full README is not stored in the case; only short field-specific evidence excerpts and comparison results are retained. Results remain descriptive signals until reviewed in the existing assessment and Data Steward workflow.
Guidance provenance: README generation and README-specific rules are informed by the EPFL RDM Team README best-practices guide and template (2022) and the 4TU.ResearchData Guidelines for creating a README file (July 2020). The toolkit applies these as evidence-based preparation guidance, not as automatic repository acceptance criteria.

About the FAIR Data Clinic Toolkit

Purpose, proof-of-concept boundaries, and current limitations.

About this toolkit

The FAIR Data Clinic Toolkit is a standalone proof of concept for pre-deposit Dataset Reuse Readiness assessment with a shared assessment core and multiple continuation paths. Its primary function is to inspect and evaluate the files, documentation, metadata, provenance, software, rights, access information, and relationships that constitute a research data package while those elements can still be corrected before repository deposit.

Researchers can resolve routine preparation findings themselves, record clarification, reassess corrected files, finish assessment-only, request Data Steward assistance, or prepare for a repository when no professional block remains. Data Steward or specialist review is mandatory only for issues that require professional judgment or governance authority.

dev8 preserves the twelve repository-neutral reuse-readiness dimensions, the artifact and evidence layers, the governed rule engine, expanded cross-artifact reasoning, researcher remediation, canonical outputs, and evidence-bound professional review. It adds a deterministic Canonical Publication Object as the controlled publication boundary, an explicit field-authority and exclusion model, relationship-aware package descriptions, repository-neutral validation, and offline mapping reports for future adapters. 4TU.ResearchData, Zenodo, and Dataverse are mapping-fixture targets only: no credentials, live repository connection, DOI action, or file transfer is implemented. The CPO is designed for later Schema.org, DataCite, DCAT, RO-Crate, repository-adapter, and discovery-catalog projections without making any external standard the Clinic's internal canonical model.

README guidance provenance: The generated README structure and deterministic README checks are informed by the EPFL RDM Team README best-practices guide and template (2022), which cites the 4TU.ResearchData Guidelines for creating a README file (July 2020). These sources inform preparation guidance; they do not create repository acceptance or institutional approval.

README Documentation Completeness: The toolkit operationalizes applicable README guidance into two transparent coverage measures: core completeness for strongly recommended elements and overall documentation coverage for core plus supporting elements. No arbitrary point weighting is used. Not-applicable and not-assessed elements are excluded from the denominator, and conflicts remain visible separately.

Assessment prior art: The toolkit credits the CABI FAIR Process Framework Data Self-Assessment Tool for selected dataset-maturity, metadata-persistence, semantic-vocabulary, personal-data/licensing, and decomposed-provenance concepts. The Clinic independently implements evidence-based pre-deposit preparation controls and does not adopt CABI’s agricultural FAIR scoring model.
Lineage: CABI credits the DANS SATIFYD tool (2019). DANS identifies FAIR-Aware as the supported successor to SATIFYD. The ARDC FAIR Data Self-Assessment Tool is recorded as related educational prior art. These sources inform positioning, educational progress presentation, and rule concepts; none confers institutional authority or repository acceptance.
dev8 boundary: this build creates a repository-neutral publication projection and offline mapping contract. It does not authenticate reviewer identity, confer institutional authority, make automatic legal/privacy/ethics/security decisions, implement live repository APIs or credentials, transfer dataset files, mint DOIs, provide production collaboration, assess scientific validity, calculate a FAIR score, or implement the future discovery catalog.

Built and maintained by Richard Dennis. UI assisted by ChatGPT.

How the POC works

Files are selected and analyzed locally in the browser. The assessment produces evidence signals and preparation actions; researchers can correct routine issues, reassess the package, and then choose self-service completion, Data Steward assistance, or repository preflight. Shared work is simulated by exporting and importing a structured JSON case handoff. The handoff contains case information, findings, comments, decisions, status, and audit history; it does not create a shared institutional workspace.

Local processing is not the same as an approved secure environment. Browser case storage is not encrypted, names and email addresses are personal data, and manifests, checksums, findings, comments, and entered metadata may remain on the workstation. Use fictitious contacts and non-sensitive or explicitly approved files. Delete cases through Manage all cases and clear the browser site data when the local test record is no longer required.

Repository preflight and dev8 mapping previews are simulated locally. No metadata or files are transmitted to 4TU.ResearchData, Zenodo, Dataverse, JSM, Research Cockpit, or RAPS. A future institutional implementation would require authentication, approved storage, role-based permissions, retention rules, records-management decisions, secure repository credentials, and formal security, privacy, accessibility, and service-owner review.

Known limitations

  • No authentication or real multi-user access.
  • No server-side storage, notifications, or real-time collaboration.
  • Selected file contents are not retained after the browser session.
  • Export/import simulates handoff and can create version-management risk if users exchange the wrong revision.
  • Technical findings and assessment signals remain pre-deposit evidence, not a FAIR certification, scientific-quality determination, legal decision, or repository-acceptance decision.
  • The README Documentation Completeness percentage measures applicable documentation coverage only. It is not a dataset reusability score or readiness percentage.
  • Production shared Data Steward service is not implemented. dev7 records evidence-bound professional review locally and uses explicit export/handoff; it provides no authentication, notifications, real-time collaboration, or institutional authorization.
  • The repository-preflight foundation is not connected to 4TU.ResearchData or Zenodo. This development build does not create live repository drafts, upload files, reserve DOIs through an API, or synchronize repository metadata.
  • No live JSM, Research Cockpit, RAPS, Zenodo, Dataverse, or other repository integration.

Accessible change log

Major development changes from the locked v3.0 baseline onward.

v3.0 - Full FAIR Clinic workflow baseline

Introduced Researcher and Data Steward modes, manual FAIR assessment, action generation, templates, repository routing, conditional RAPS preparation, FAIR checks, and local case storage.

v3.1 - UX simplification experiment

Added progressive disclosure, guided start, progress indicators, case dashboard, compact assessment views, and clearer navigation.

v3.2 - DMP/JSM handoff experiment

Explored structured import, mapping, conflict detection, selective application, and JSM-ready outputs without a live connection.

v4.0 - Institutional integration prototype

Tested authentication, permissions, audit logging, controlled updates, and integration boundaries in a mock institutional architecture.

v4.0.1 - UX-first integration experiment

Reduced the visible workflow and hid advanced integration controls, but did not replace the locked v3.0 baseline.

v5.0 beta - Researcher-focused redesign

Shifted from a manual checklist to local package analysis, generated actions and templates, reassessment, repository guidance, and multiple cases.

v5.1 beta - Hardening baseline

Added IndexedDB, stronger governance gating, improved parsing, archive inspection, evidence and confidence, persistent templates, and clearer reassessment.

v5.2 beta - Domain and repository profiles

Added specialist package profiles, repository preparation profiles, structured metadata, and separate review and deposit packages.

v5.3 - Controlled pilot and requirements discovery

Added pilot evidence, finding validation, missed-issue reporting, Data Steward review outcomes, and a reference test corpus. Locked as the final requirements-discovery prototype.

v5.4 - Combined workflow proof of concept

Introduced researcher and Data Steward role views, shared case structure, conditional intake, submission and resubmission, comments, change requests, optional consultation, specialist referral, repository confirmation, case states, audit history, and export/import handoff. No new scoring framework was included.

v5.4.1 - Combined-workflow POC baseline

Locked as the proof-of-concept baseline for the combined Researcher and Data Steward workflow, including submission, review, comments, resubmission, audit history, and simulated JSON handoff.

v5.5 - Assessment-model pilot

Introduced multiple package components and assessment profiles, the Dataset Content and Reuse Readiness rubric, structured researcher evidence and Data Steward decisions, 4TU.ResearchData metadata-readiness rules, curator-style improvement output, separate handoff and backup exports, and a canonical package record prepared for future interoperability. Full RO-Crate generation remains deferred.

v5.5.1 RC1 - Assessment corrections

Aligned Research Cockpit project stages, added two curator-derived 4TU.ResearchData recommendations with explicit provenance, enforced all eight handoff checks, changed the default evidence basis to Not recorded, required rationale for material Data Steward overrides, and corrected skipped-checksum handling.

v5.5.1 RC2 - Workflow, repository, migration, and pilot hardening

Made the Data Steward repository direction authoritative throughout assessment and package generation; added immediate repository-dependent rerendering; corrected documentation-only integrity handling; introduced explicit specialist-review resolution states; enforced allowed workflow transitions; added controlled post-submission locking; strengthened import validation and legacy Research Cockpit stage migration; replaced the misleading linear timeline with recorded status history; activated the pilot record; strengthened final package validation; improved modal keyboard behavior and focus restoration; and added stale-analysis safeguards. The combined Researcher and Data Steward workflow and the 12-criterion assessment model remain intact.

v5.5.1 RC3 - FAIR-mapping and consistency corrections

Corrected the automated-findings FAIR mapping so that licensing and rights signals map to Reusable (R1.1) rather than Accessible; exempted metadata-only records from the restricted-access Creative Commons block, so a metadata-only CC0 record is no longer flagged as conflicting; standardized the repository-route label to "Disciplinary repository" across the researcher and Data Steward views; and normalized the remaining British spellings to American English. The combined Researcher and Data Steward workflow and the 12-criterion assessment model are unchanged.

v5.6 - Interface housekeeping

Locked v5.5.1 RC3 and opened the v5.6 line. Applied title-case to case-context and workflow status labels; added a reset action to clear the current case; added a "Contact the Data Steward" option; added a TU/e favicon and an MIT License notice in the footer. No changes to the assessment logic, rubric, data schema, or stored-case compatibility.

v5.7 - Integrity and export separation (in progress)

Removed internal Data Steward workflow data from the repository deposit package, replacing it with a sanitized public preparation statement; added checksum-and-manifest coverage validation for file-based deposit packages; set the ZIP UTF-8 filename flag (general-purpose bit 11). Further integrity items — deposit-mode readiness gate, imported ready/closed revalidation, and audit-event validation — are tracked for subsequent v5.7 increments. Added a department pull-down to the Contact action so the researcher selects the appropriate data steward (source: rdm.tue.nl/docs/contact), with central RDM fallback. No changes to the assessment rubric.

v5.7.1 RC2 - State integrity and authority hardening

Added explicit deposit-mode gates; quarantined imported authoritative states; validated audit and status-history events; restricted reset and duplication; preserved improvement actions; invalidated stale decisions after reassessment; separated public deposit conditions from internal rationale; added restorable workspace backups; strengthened checksum overrides, ZIP paths, CSV safety, metadata validation, import limits, persistent error summaries, and browser integrity self-tests. The 12-criterion assessment model remains unchanged.

v5.7.1 RC3 - Workflow closure and readiness reconciliation

Added a Data-Steward-authorized closed-without-deposit terminal state with structured closure outcomes and mandatory rationale; introduced explicit finding-to-rubric mappings and professional finding dispositions; made unresolved professional findings a direct repository-readiness block; removed the circular workflow-status dependency from finding resolution; retained complete authoritative audit and status histories while limiting only the visible history panels; and added persistent, dynamically counted integrity self-check reporting. The 12-criterion assessment model remains unchanged.

v5.7.1 RC4 Corrected - Interface, governance, and diagnostic hardening

Retains the RC4 interface refresh and adds a defensive Data Steward role check for closure without deposit, aligned 4TU source provenance with explicit review-due metadata, version-scoped automatic integrity testing, stale-result detection, and persistent failed-test details. The integrity suite contains 18 checks, including the closure role boundary. No changes were made to the 12-criterion assessment model.

v5.8.0-dev1 - Readiness consistency correction

Corrected the consistency validator so automated pass findings remain evidence and do not require a Data Steward disposition before a related rubric criterion can be marked Demonstrated. The complete unrestricted Researcher-to-Data-Steward workflow passed the release-critical retest.

v5.8.0-dev2 - Structured Data Steward assignment and routing

Replaced free-text department and assignment entry with controlled department and Data Steward selection, explicit assignment confirmation, directory-backed contact details, historical assignment snapshots, central-support and manual fallbacks, Data Steward override controls, authoritative case-based email routing, stale-directory warnings, and migration of legacy free-text assignments. The assessment model and readiness logic are unchanged.

v5.8.0-dev3 - Institutional application home and role dashboards

Added the institutional application home, explicit Researcher and Data Steward entry paths, role-specific task cards, recent-case navigation, pre-assessment guidance, and a Home return control while preserving the RC3 operational workflow, structured Data Steward assignment, case schema, findings, rubric, handoffs, readiness, and closure controls.

v5.8.0-dev4 - Guided assessment experience

Integrated the ARDC-style educational interaction model throughout the Researcher assessment: pre-assessment tabs, four thematic views over the validated 12 criteria, persistent progress, section and focus modes, contextual definitions, evidence-linked corrective guidance, a traceable assessment result profile, and a downloadable assessment summary. The case schema, automated findings, Data Steward rubric, handoff, readiness, and closure logic remain authoritative and unchanged.

v5.8.0-rc1 - Guided assessment, institutional home, and release renumbering

Restored the complete application footer on the institutional home, corrected the change log to include RC4 in strict release sequence, reduced and corrected the capitalization of the home-page title, updated visible and internal release identifiers, and completed a backward-preservation audit against the preceding development builds, and renumbered the release line to a single monotonic identifier (v5.8.0-rc1) after the nested release-candidate numbering was found to be ambiguous. No assessment, assignment, storage, handoff, readiness, or closure logic was changed.

v5.8.0-rc2 - Feature preservation and reset visibility correction

Restored the complete Case menu on the institutional home and added a direct Reset Draft action that is visible only while the current case remains eligible for reset. The existing reset guard, confirmation, audit event, case identifier preservation, and post-submission restrictions remain unchanged. A backward-preservation audit confirmed that all control identifiers and named application functions from v5.7.1 RC4 Corrected, v5.8.0-dev2, v5.8.0-dev3, and v5.8.0-dev4 remain present. No assessment, assignment, storage, handoff, readiness, or closure logic was removed.

v5.8.0-rc3 - Schema.org JSON-LD restoration

Restored machine-readable Schema.org Dataset JSON-LD generation as a first-class Researcher and Data Steward output. Added live preview, copy and download controls; public-field mapping for creators, ORCIDs, affiliation, identifiers, repository, access, rights, methods, temporal and spatial coverage, related resources, and file-level DataDownload distributions; JSON-LD inclusion in both review and repository-preparation packages; format-aware generated-document downloads; and integrity checks that distinguish this output from deferred full RO-Crate generation. No internal comments, professional deliberation, or dataset file contents are included in the JSON-LD export.

v5.8.0-rc4 - Generated-output workspace and JSON-LD placement correction

Reestablished the v5.3-style generated-output workspace as the primary location for reusable case outputs. Promoted Schema.org JSON-LD to the first generated output; added output-specific descriptions, filenames, format labels, completeness diagnostics, live read-only JSON-LD generation, refresh, copy, and format-correct download behavior; added direct Researcher, Data Steward, home-dashboard, and Case-menu access to the shared output workspace; reduced Step 5 to metadata validation and package inclusion; retained secondary preview and direct-download routes; and preserved the rc3 generator, privacy boundary, package inclusion, workflow, assessment, assignment, reset, footer, and change-log controls.

v5.8.0-rc5 - Deterministic cross-artifact consistency review

Added a local, deterministic consistency engine that compares README claims with the authoritative public metadata, Schema.org JSON-LD, and file manifest without using an external AI service or numerical score. Added 15 evidence-traceable rules; source-line excerpts; Researcher actions; Data Steward reconciliation with evidence-bound dispositions and rationale; readiness gates for unresolved repository-blocking conflicts; audit events for every comparison; review-package reports; guided-criterion evidence integration; and regression tests for license, access, creator, version, identifier, file, checksum, dictionary, software, and privacy boundaries. The existing 12-criterion assessment remains authoritative.

v5.8.0-rc6 - EPFL/4TU README alignment extension

Extended the deterministic cross-artifact registry from 15 to 28 rules using the EPFL RDM Team README best-practices guide and its cited 4TU README guidance as explicit provenance sources. Added funding, terms of use, citation instructions, processing methods, collection period, calibration and technical parameters, practical reuse instructions, quality assurance, standards and vocabularies, update history, README root placement, README file format, and ISO-aware date, language, and country normalization. Added structured metadata fields, Schema.org mappings, profile-aware applicability, evidence-bound Data Steward reconciliation, updated generated README guidance, package-report provenance, and regression coverage. No numerical score, AI service, or new authority model was introduced.

v5.8.0-rc7 - Dataset maturity, semantic vocabulary, provenance, and governance extension

Added Dataset maturity stage as a separate case-context dimension without altering Research Cockpit stage, FAIR Data Clinic activity, or controlled workflow status. Added maturity-aware rule applicability; structured repeatable semantic-vocabulary records for metadata, data values, units, reference data, classifications, provenance, and resource types; decomposed provenance fields and evidence rules for data origin, reused-data citations, collection or generation workflow, processing history, and version history; an evidence-bound personal or sensitive data versus open-access and unrestricted-license contradiction gate; repository metadata-persistence profiles with source and review dates; and nonnumeric criterion-level reassessment comparison. Added CABI FAIR Process Framework, DANS SATIFYD, FAIR-Aware, and ARDC prior-art provenance while retaining EPFL and 4TU README credits. Updated public metadata, Schema.org JSON-LD, review packages, handoffs, backups, audit history, help text, footer, change log, migration messages, and integrity tests. No FAIR score, badge, external AI call, or new approval authority was introduced.

v5.8.0-rc8 - README Documentation Completeness

Added evidence-based README Documentation Completeness as a separate documentation-coverage measure, not a FAIR score or repository-readiness percentage. Core completeness uses applicable strongly recommended EPFL/4TU-aligned elements; overall coverage includes core and supporting elements without arbitrary weighting. Added maturity- and profile-aware denominators, explicit complete, partial, missing, conflicting, requires-confirmation, not-applicable, and not-assessed states, source-traceable element reports, researcher and Data Steward workspaces, percentage and element-level change comparison, review-package exports, audit events, and dedicated regression coverage. Preserved the 12-criterion model, 37 deterministic rules, cross-artifact evidence, governance gates, public/internal export separation, and Data Steward authority.

v5.8.0-rc9 - Cross-browser package selection and role-specific information architecture

Added explicit folder, multiple-file, ZIP-package, drag-and-drop, and documentation-only selection paths with browser-capability guidance and Safari-oriented fallback instructions. Reframed the Researcher review stage around plain-language priorities, information needed from the researcher, items for Data Steward review, and progressively disclosed technical evidence while preserving the full 12-criterion assessment and automated findings. Added maturity-aware priority labels, an accessible seven-section deposit preparation interface, and a scoped Data Steward console with persistent case context, readiness blockers, role-specific tabs, and a fixed decision bar that proxies the existing authoritative controls. Refreshed the public 4TU README guidance link while retaining the historical source identifier for stored-report compatibility. Preserved every RC8 control identifier, named function, assessment rule, data schema, workflow state, export boundary, privacy boundary, and Data Steward authority model.

v5.8.0-rc10 - Full UI integration attempt

Applied the approved UI direction directly to the working toolkit rather than only borrowing selected interaction patterns. The Researcher review stage now uses the approved card language, pill-based status cues, calmer progressive disclosure, and a clearly separated advanced evidence view. The Data Steward review workspace now uses the approved console framing, refined metadata strip, compact readiness gate, visually integrated review tabs, and anchored decision bar. Updated the proof-of-concept strip, footer, release metadata, and visible release identifiers to rc10 while preserving the validated RC9 workflow, assessment logic, package-selection routes, public and internal export boundaries, and Data Steward authority.

v5.8.0-rc11 - Complete working UI implementation and audit corrections

Implemented the attached Researcher deposit information architecture and Data Steward console as working application structures rather than styling overlays. The Researcher retains a five-step spine and now uses seven live Deposit sections with grouped metadata, integrated documentation, vocabularies, provenance, grouped consistency results, generated outputs, and package preparation. The Data Steward uses an eight-section nonsequential console with persistent case context, readiness blockers, evidence and disposition controls, and a fixed decision bar. Added live Researcher response controls, completed-check disclosure, and permanent FDC UI namespace aliases while retaining legacy rc9 implementation names only for compatibility. Corrected the stale migration provenance string, replaced display-none file inputs with browser-reachable off-screen inputs, verified the current 4TU README guidance URL and July 2020 label, and updated all visible and internal release identifiers, footer text, help text, and self-tests to rc11.

v5.8.0-rc12 - Data Steward routing and accessibility CSS maintenance

Remapped the Data Steward README Documentation Completeness and criterion-level reassessment sections to the Rubric console panel, matching their authoritative DOM placement and preventing future section links from falling back to Overview. Consolidated the duplicate visually-hidden accessibility rule into one canonical declaration. Added permanent regression self-tests for both section mappings and for the single visually-hidden declaration. Updated the release identity to rc12 without changing the assessment model, workflow states, schemas, package-selection behavior, export boundaries, privacy boundary, or Data Steward authority.

v5.8.0-rc13 - RC12 corrective release

Resolved Mariana Menegon’s RC1 feedback and the documented RC12 post-publication review findings. Removed the persistent header role switch; consolidated the duplicated guidance entry points into one assessment-guide modal; clarified the local-processing and sensitive-data boundary; aligned the Prepare-step Continue state with all required fields; corrected stale primary-type component selection; strengthened the Run automated checks call to action; distinguished automated technical evidence from the Technical usability assessment theme; made Improvement theme navigation explicit; explained the Data Steward contribution at submission; corrected ownership, institutional-record, and signed-backup terminology; added accessible names and tab-order controls for hidden file inputs; removed incomplete ARIA menu semantics; prevented automatic creation of an untitled saved case; exposed the embedded Data Steward directory as a dated snapshot; and added reproducible build, validation, environment, and release-packaging assets. A later RC14 audit confirmed the role-switch and single-modal claims, but found that the guide tabs still lacked complete tab-to-panel relationships and that one current Data Steward sentence still used “approved console design.” Those two residual issues are corrected in RC14. The assessment model, workflow states, export boundaries, and Data Steward authority remain unchanged.

v5.8.0-rc14 - Progressive disclosure and changelog verification

Introduced an accessible progressive-disclosure system without deleting guidance: Essential, Standard, and Detailed display levels; reusable contextual information controls for field-level guidance; mouse, keyboard, focus, click, tap, Escape, and outside-click operation; mobile bottom-sheet positioning; and preservation of decision-critical warnings and validation messages. Completed the five assessment-guide tabs with unique identifiers, aria-controls, aria-selected, roving tabindex, associated tab panels, and arrow-key navigation. Audited RC13’s current changelog claims against the artifact, confirmed removal of the persistent header role switch and consolidation to one guide modal, corrected the incomplete tab-semantics implication, and removed the residual “approved console design” wording. Added dedicated regression tests and a changelog-claim audit record. No assessment criterion, deterministic rule, workflow state, schema, export boundary, or Data Steward authority was changed.

v5.8.0-rc15 - Final stabilization candidate

Finalized the 5.8 release-candidate line before v5.9 development. Clarified that the primary current function is pre-deposit Dataset Content and Reuse Readiness assessment and that repository preparation is downstream. Added a researcher-facing status guide and standardized actionable finding presentation around what was found, why it matters for reuse, what to do, the evidence basis, and the assessment boundary. Clarified the existing “I need help” response as a Data Steward-help request without changing workflow routing. Corrected stale About text, strengthened local-processing and repository-connection boundaries, and explicitly stated that the current 4TU preparation panel does not synchronize with 4TU.ResearchData. Added RC15 stabilization regression checks. No assessment criterion, deterministic rule, workflow state, schema, repository rule, export boundary, privacy boundary, or Data Steward authority was changed; the v5.9 reuse-engine redesign, conditional Data Steward routing, canonical evidence model, and live repository adapters remain out of scope.

v5.9.0-dev1 - Application and UI foundation

Branched directly from locked v5.8.0-rc15 and retained its stabilized package selection, deterministic analysis, cross-artifact checks, generated outputs, migration safeguards, accessibility structures, export boundaries, and browser integrity suite. Introduced a new isolated v5.9 storage namespace, repository-neutral canonical artifact/evidence/finding record, twelve v5.9 reuse-readiness dimensions, explicit legacy criterion mapping, multi-path workflow foundation, assessment-only completion, voluntary scoped Data Steward assistance, professional-blocking detection, repository-preflight targets for 4TU.ResearchData and Zenodo, and a post-assessment Next actions interface. The former 4TU-specific core criterion was moved to repository preflight and replaced by Cross-artifact coherence in the core twelve. No live repository transfer, production authentication, or shared institutional service is implemented in dev1.

v5.9.0-dev2 - Artifact inspection and variable documentation

Extended the validated dev1 application foundation with bounded local artifact-aware inspection for README, CSV/TSV, XLSX, structured JSON/YAML/XML metadata, and data dictionaries. Added a persistent Variable Documentation Workspace that detects columns and workbook sheets, records structural/type evidence without persisting sampled row values, aligns matching data-dictionary entries, captures definitions, units, codes/categories, and missing-value semantics, and exports a reusable data-dictionary CSV. Introduced the first native RR inspection-rule subset and connected preparation-blocking inspection findings to repository-preflight gating. Expanded the synthetic benchmark corpus and updated later repository architecture so dev8 models scoped authorization capabilities and dev11 supports bidirectional Dataverse external-tool entry plus high-level curation-status synchronization. No live repository transfer, automatic publication, or production shared Data Steward service is implemented.

v5.9.0-dev3 - Computational artifact inspection and structured documentation intelligence

Extended dev2 with bounded local inspection of source code, Jupyter notebooks, dependency/environment records, and scientific-container header signals; added DataverseNO README template detection, embedded-version and filename-version comparison, exact field-anchor extraction, placeholder scanning, and metadata/repository delegation recognition; prevented recognized delegation from becoming false-positive legacy cross-artifact missing-value results; extended variable documentation with decimal separator, value labels, source, and specialized-format/abbreviation fields; added artifact relationships, file-level change provenance, structured people/organization/funder identifiers, quality-assurance evidence, and an appropriate-nondisclosure disposition model. These additions acquire evidence only; governed dev4 gate policy and dev5 rule expansion remain deferred.

v5.9.0-dev4 - Governed native Reuse Readiness rule engine

Introduces a governed machine-readable RR rule registry with stable rule versions, responsibility classes, assessment phases, maturity and package-profile applicability, evidence authority, source relationships, external alignments, policy strength, explicit remediation and verification. Adds deterministic tabular structure rules, computational-reuse rules, quality-assurance and identifier recommendations, appropriate-nondisclosure and attestation records, and a four-class rule-fixture contract. A pre-lock correction records dev3 as the immediate development predecessor, binds inherited native RR findings to the dev4 governance contract, distinguishes active from explicitly deferred rules, preserves researcher attestations, and prevents false computational-documentation findings when structured README evidence is present. No repository API, FAIR score, live transfer, or dev5 cross-artifact expansion is introduced.

v5.9.0-dev5 - Expanded Cross-Artifact Reasoning

Added package-level reasoning across README, manifest, dictionaries, tabular schemas, metadata, code, environments, rights/access, provenance, identifiers, quality-assurance evidence, temporal/spatial signals and file-level change history. Introduced explicit relationship outcomes, both-sides evidence, delegation-aware metadata resolution, nondisclosure-aware suppression, maturity/responsibility inheritance, activated computational input/output counterpart checks, mutation tests, and an explicit dev4-to-dev5 test-migration registry.

v5.9.0-dev6 - Researcher remediation UX and canonical outputs

Branched from corrected dev5 checksum 445a68203d0e9d34eb4d59a8274ab19dd9187615433b46e79ac1e2a5274d3a10. Adds an evidence-preserving remediation lifecycle, explicit comparative reassessment states (new, unchanged, improved, resolved, reopened), prior-evidence and prior-finding-version snapshots, six explicit finding-to-action routes, appropriate-nondisclosure and Data Steward routing controls, deterministic one-way generated outputs with explicit authority classes and generation provenance, a dev5→dev6 predecessor-test migration registry, and a standalone TU/e interface aligned visually with Research Cockpit. Generated outputs are read-only projections in the Clinic and never silently mutate canonical case state. A pre-lock exit-gate correction makes explicit README access labels consumable by RR-XA-ACC-001 and ensures reopened shared-professional findings return to professional-review-required rather than researcher action-needed. No repository API, production authentication, scientific-validity judgment, or FAIR score is introduced.

v5.9.0-dev7 - Professional review, Data Steward assistance, and evidence-bound reporting

Branched only from locked dev6 checksum fcff57fc7a34312aaebcbf5b0ec71587aa958dc7060685171df3e1e1e4430771. Preserves the dev6 remediation and canonical-output authority model and adds evidence-cycle-bound professional review requests, scoped assistance intake, specialist routing, immutable professional observations, return-to-researcher dispositions, current-evidence professional determinations, and JSON/Markdown professional-review reports. A professional determination may resolve only the matching current evidence cycle; later reassessment can reopen the finding and creates a new review request. Pre-lock exit-gate corrections clarify that routine assessment and remediation are self-service while the separate repository-ready confirmation remains a Data Steward-controlled proof-of-concept step, and preserve an open professional-review request across deterministic re-renders so sequential guidance and determination can be recorded through the visible Data Steward interface. A final release-presentation correction orders the v5.9 development changelog sequentially and adds automated changelog chronology and uniqueness checks to the browser integrity suite. The proof of concept does not authenticate reviewers or confer institutional authority. No repository API, dev8 adapter, FTR integration, FAIR score, production collaboration service, or automatic legal/privacy/ethics/security decision is introduced.

v5.9.0-dev8 - Canonical Publication Object and repository-neutral handoff

Branched only from corrected locked dev7 checksum f60c08f63a1e1b6878ebcd62a908deab9a71b6fb87182ff3c7e4e75d79ca2d3a and preserves all 314 predecessor-test obligations. Adds a deterministic allowlist-based Canonical Publication Object, explicit field-authority and publication-class mapping, privacy and internal-workflow exclusions, package-relative artifact descriptions, relationship-aware provenance, repository-neutral validation states, capability declarations, and deterministic offline mapping reports for 4TU.ResearchData, Zenodo, and Dataverse fixtures. The researcher-facing handoff UI uses plain language and keeps CPO/schema detail under progressive disclosure. No live repository API, authentication, credential handling, file transfer, DOI action, production backend, catalog implementation, FAIR score, or automatic professional decision is introduced.

v5.9.0-dev9 - Offline 4TU.ResearchData adapter pilot

Branched only from locked dev8 checksum a3c99063b606db2ca2208a7abdfa660589a654b4a7b20ce6da1ac45273ce68bd. Preserves the dev8 CPO schema and one-way authority boundary while adding the locked deterministic offline 4TU mapping report, frozen vocabulary provenance, target-required gaps, and professional or canonical handoff blockers. No live repository connection, credentials, DOI operation, file transfer, submission, repository write-back, FAIR score, certification, or acceptance claim is introduced.
